title: Padded and Bounded Witnesses
statement: Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a language of binary strings, and let $x$ be a binary string. There exists a binary string $v$ of length $(C+1)(|x|+1)^c$ such that $xv\in V^{\mathrm{pad}}_{C,c}$ if and only if there exists a binary string $u$ with $|u|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ and $\langle x,u\rangle\in V$, where $\langle x,u\rangle$ is obtained by doubling each bit of $x$, appending $01$, and then appending $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of binary strings
replaced:
Let $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$, and let
$V^{\mathrm{pad}}_{C,c}$ be the set of binary strings $y$ such that, for the least
$n$ with $n + (C+1)(n+1)^c = |y|$ (which must exist), the suffix $v$ of $y$ after
its first $n$ bits contains a $1$, and the prefix $u$ of $v$ preceding its last
$1$ satisfies $|u| \le C(n+1)^c$ and $\langle x, u\rangle \in V$, where $x$ is
the first $n$ bits of $y$ and $\langle x, u\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair
encoding ($x$ with every bit doubled, then $01$, then $u$). Then for every binary
string $x$, there exists $v$ with $|v| = (C+1)(|x|+1)^c$ and
$xv \in V^{\mathrm{pad}}_{C,c}$ if and only if there exists $u$ with
$|u| \le C(|x|+1)^c$ and $\langle x, u\rangle \in V$.
